subject: Ephemeral Boost Addendum — pricing & cooldown structure
messages:
From: J. Turner <j.turner@acme-analytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ephemeral capacity for Q4 load spike — can we get a short-term option?

Hi Rachel,

We're forecasting a sizeable but short (2–3 week) model inference spike in early October tied to a seasonal campaign. Our infra team would prefer not to commit to a larger reserved pool for the year; instead we're exploring an "ephemeral boost" addendum — temporary dedicated headroom that attaches to our existing Dedicated capacity with clear cooldowns and surge rates.

Questions:
- What are the typical ephemeral boost sizing granularity (GPUs / vGPU units)?
- How do you measure/charge surge tokens vs. committed throughput?
- Can we get a guaranteed throughput floor during a boost window (min p99 latency targets)?
- Are cooldowns applied per customer or per pool, and what are the exception paths?

We'd like a short proposal we can share with procurement that includes price brackets and a rough SOW outline (DocuSign-friendly).

Thanks — JT
J. Turner
Head of Platform, ACME Analytics

[Attachment: forecast_q4_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: J. Turner <j.turner@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ephemeral capacity for Q4 load spike — can we get a short-term option?

JT — thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. Short answer: yes, we can do an ephemeral boost addendum. I've sketched an initial framing below and looped in Karthik (serving/runtime) and Monica (pricing/procurement) for details and a numbers-backed sheet.

Proposal sketch (high level):
- Term: attach to your existing Dedicated contract as an addendum; minimum window 7 days, up to 28 days per activation.
- Sizing: billed in "GPU-headroom units" (1 unit = one A100-equivalent GPU-hour). We can price by unit slabs (small, medium, large) and also allow an elastic slider for minute-level consumption (higher per-unit rate).
- Throughput SLA during active window: best-effort to maintain your current p95/p99 targets; we can guarantee a throughput floor (tokens/sec) if you pre-declare workload mix and max seq length.
- Cooldown & governance: cooldown is applied at the account level (sliding 30-day moving window) to prevent repeated bursts; exceptions are possible via emergency top-ups with higher short-term surcharge.

Next steps: Monica will propose 2–3 pricing tiers + a sample SOW PDF. Karthik will confirm any technical limits that would affect guaranteed latency. Once you review, we can produce a DocuSign addendum and a one-page SOW.

Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Signature: Rachel Kim | Senior Solutions Engineer | rachel_kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: J. Turner <j.turner@acme-analytics.com>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ephemeral capacity for Q4 load spike — can we get a short-term option?

Adding technical constraints and a workable guardrail set. High level notes:

- Sizing granularity: we can offer minimum 0.5 GPU-unit increments (for fractional vGPU mappings) up to whole-GPU increments. That maps well to your forecast if you give us expected concurrent streams and average seq length.
- Guaranteed throughput: we can commit to a throughput floor expressed as throughput tokens/sec per GPU-unit for the active window; guarantees require a short workload declaration (model family, avg seq, top-k settings, batching expectations).
- p99/p95: under active boost windows we aim to preserve your configured SLOs; however p99 guarantees require reserved slots in the pool and are priced higher. If you choose the "guaranteed p99" option we must allocate pinned slots in the Dedicated pool for the boost duration — this has implications for committed utilization.
- Cooldown mechanics: cooldown is account scoped. Default cooldown: equal to 2x the activation duration (e.g., 14-day cooldown for a 7-day activation) within a 90-day lookback window. Emergency exceptions: allowed with 2x surcharge and sign-off from operations.
- Failure modes and fallbacks: if capacity is constrained mid-window, requests fall back to a compatible model variant (lower-cost) or to queued handling with a configurable max queue time. We recommend including fallback policy in the SOW.

I'll supply a short appendix (technical) you can attach to the SOW describing the pinned-slot approach vs. ephemeral overlay.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Ephemeral capacity for Q4 load spike — can we get a short-term option?

Hi JT — thanks, and great to meet you. Pricing outline below (fast-following Rachel and Karthik's technical framing). I included three go-to tiers so procurement has choices; all rates are per GPU-headroom-unit-hour unless noted.

Tier A (Elastic minute-billing):
- Best for unpredictable spikes. Per-unit rate: $10.50 / GPU-unit-hour. Billed on minute granularity. No guaranteed p99; best-effort SLOs.
- Cooldown: 1.5x activation duration. 30-day rolling cap applies.

Tier B (Reserved overlay — short window):
- For customers who need predictable latency but not a long-term commit. Per-unit rate: $7.75 / GPU-unit-hour. Requires a 7-day minimum activation, 14-day cooldown. Guarantees a throughput floor, optional p95 target; p99 requires pinned slots (add-on surcharge).

Tier C (Pinned short-term reserve):
- Dedicated pinned slots during the boost (higher reliability). Per-unit rate: $12.25 / GPU-unit-hour + a one-time orchestration fee of $1,500 per activation for pool reconfiguration. Includes p99 SLA for the activation window.

Discounts / Commit tradeoffs:
- If ACME signs a 'seasonal overlay' commit (e.g., commit to 500 GPU-unit-hours over Q4), we can discount all Tier B rates by 10% and waive the orchestration fee for up to 2 activations.
- Emergency top-ups (no prior declaration): 2.5x Tier A rate, no SLA guarantees.

Attachments: I've attached a sample SOW and a working pricing workbook (ephemeral_pricing_model_v2.xlsx) showing example math for your forecast. If you want, we can run a quick model with your Q4 numbers and return an itemized quote.

Next step: if this looks directionally right, Rachel and I will produce a one-page addendum and a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: ephemeral_pricing_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)]

If we get that this week, procurement will issue a PO and we can route DocuSign. Appreciate the quick turn.

Best — JT
